source.title: Eureka-Moments in Transformers: Multi-Step Tasks Reveal Softmax Induced Optimization Problems
source.authors: David T. Hoffmann; Simon Schrodi; Jelena Bratulic; Nadine Behrmann; Volker Fischer; Thomas Brox

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures in-context-learning accuracy over training and tests whether changing the attention softmax training method affects its improvement. It does not identify or intervene on induction heads, so this is a conceptual test of ICL learning behavior rather than a direct induction-head reproduction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports GPT-2 Omniglot ICL training curves and compares baseline training with NormSoftmax. It also discusses abrupt improvements in RoBERTa language-model loss, but that is not an induction-head or ICL measurement and is not recorded as a claim-version row. Induction-head results attributed to Olsson et al. are cited background, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study trains GPT-2 on the Omniglot ICL task of Chan et al. and compares standard softmax attention with NormSoftmax. It reports that ICL accuracy and whether a sudden ICL gain occurs depend on the attention normalisation and the seed. This bears on V5, which covers ICL depending on the training setup. It never identifies, measures or ablates induction heads, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 are untested. The abrupt ICL gain is not tied to induction heads or a loss bump, so it is not a V2 test.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors' main conclusion is that transformers struggle to learn unsupervised intermediate sub-tasks, then learn them suddenly (Eureka-moments), and that this traces to softmax-induced small gradients. NormSoftmax and Heat Treatment mitigate it. The ICL (and RoBERTa) results are presented as evidence that the analysis transfers to real data, not as a study of induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not identify, measure, or ablate induction heads as in the cited original work. It trains GPT-2 with or without NormSoftmax and measures Omniglot few-shot ICL accuracy over training.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ICL outcome differs between baseline training and NormSoftmax training. Burstiness and sampling are specified as 50% and uniform, respectively, rather than varied.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 Omniglot ICL accuracy plateaus and then rises sharply (a Eureka-moment) in some seeds. The authors hypothesise this reflects multi-step learning that includes learning an induction head, but they do not measure induction heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abrupt ICL gains after a plateau occur in Omniglot ICL training, independent of any verified induction-head formation.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic two-step tasks in ViTs and single-layer transformers show sudden learning (Eureka-moments), traced to small softmax-attention gradients for W_Q and W_K. Lower temperature or NormSoftmax reduces or removes the plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abrupt attention-pattern learning in transformers can stem from softmax-induced small Q/K gradients and is modifiable by attention temperature.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235 (2024)
record.problems: The ICL evidence is presented as curves without exact accuracy values or stated uncertainty. Only two example seed curves are shown, although the average is over 4 seeds. The paper does not directly measure induction heads, so it cannot establish their formation or causal role.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were omitted. RoBERTa language-model loss results are outside the measured behaviors specified by these claim versions.

untested.parts: No previous-token heads, head composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] analysis.
No induction-head detection over training, no token-index loss and no loss-bump coincidence. Only Omniglot ICL accuracy curves are shown.
No attribution of ICL to induction heads and no large models.
No survey of induction heads across families, sizes or runs.

Induction-head formation is not measured. Data properties (burstiness fixed at 50%, uniform sampling) are not varied. ICL persistence over long training is not assessed. Only the attention-normalisation choice is varied.
Does not separate copying from task learning or identify other carrier heads.
No decomposition of induction-head formation into sub-steps.

record.verdict_notes: The study's own ICL result rests only on Fig. 9b curves (4 seeds, 2 shown, no numbers). Its references to induction heads are cited background from Olsson et al. The V5 link is weak: the setup variable is attention normalisation, not data properties, and induction heads are never observed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not analyze previous-token heads, head composition, or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying mechanism.

The study measures ICL accuracy over training but does not measure induction-head formation, token-index loss, or whether an induction-head transition coincides with an ICL gain and a training-loss bump.
It does not attribute most ICL to induction heads or test that attribution in large transformers.
It does not survey induction behavior across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
It tests a training-method change on Omniglot ICL performance, but not induction-head formation, data-property variation, or whether ICL persists across those data properties.
It does not distinguish copying from few-shot task learning by testing other heads or mechanisms as the main carrier.
It does not decompose induction-head formation into sub-steps or test for multiple transitions in induction-head formation.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. The ICL evidence is figure-only, without exact accuracies or reported uncertainty; it does not establish induction-head formation, timing, or causality.

statements.correction: GPT-2 on Omniglot; NormSoftmax yields higher ICL accuracy than baseline and seems to prevent absent or small Eureka-moments; averages over 4 seeds; exact accuracies unstated; induction-head formation unmeasured.
statements.problem: R2 is cited for a statement about circuit formation, but this study measures ICL accuracy without identifying or measuring induction-head formation. The paragraph omits this study's actual result; its numerical claims concern other studies.
